problem:
An eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}]$ 
corresponding to an eigenvalue $\lambda =5k-4$ is $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3k-1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix

feedback.problem: The eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ -k & -1\end{aligned}]$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =k-1$ is  $[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ -k & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =(k-1)[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-16 \\ -4k+4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4k-4 \\ -4k+4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-16=4k-4, \\ -4k+4=-4k+4\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
-12=4k\,⟹\,k=-3.
$$

The second equation is true for any value of $k.$

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=-3.$
